utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The evidence will show that at that time, on the 1st of October, 1991, Vojislav Seselj and his associates in the SRS and SCP already cooperated fully with the JNA and the leaderships in the regions in recruiting, transferring, and engaging volunteers on the front lines, in particular, in relation to Vukovar and Dubrovnik. Were the goals of the JCE regarding the Serb territories in Croatia achieved? Unfortunately, yes. We will hear from witnesses, including an expert, about the demographic changes in the SAOs in Croatia that left the claimed areas basically free of non-Serbs, in particular Croats. The western borders along the Karlobag-Ogulin-Karlovac-Virovitica line were not achieved fully given the resistance of the Croatian forces, but they were achieved almost. Seselj himself said on the 6th of March, 1992, in a TV interview in Belgrade, that will be Exhibit 1849 the following: "Well, I am of the opinion that we did not manage to achieve that ideal western border of ours: Karlobag-Ogulin-Karlovac-Virovitica. We did not succeed with Karlobag, but we are somewhere in the vicinity of the former Maslenicki Bridge, and that is several kilometres away from Karlobag. We did not succeed with Ogulin; however, we are close to Ogulin. We did not succeed with Karlovac; however, we are holding the suburbs of Karlovac. We did not succeed with Virovitica, but we are holding the suburbs of Pakrac, one part of Pakrac and parts of Western Slavonia." Let me show you now a map that's the official map of the RSK. It's Exhibit 2829. It's a bit hard to see, but if you follow the brownish lines, you can see, first --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you tell us which number this is in the bundle?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: It's 2829 -- oh, in the bundle, I'm sorry. It's number 10.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And the translation -- there is quite some text on it, and the translation is 10A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You can see here actually outlined the achievements in relation to the SAOs, Eastern Slavonia, Western Slavonia, and the SAO Krajina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: By the end of 1991, given the military and political situation on the ground, the focus of the JCE shifted to Bosnia and Herzegovina. In a conference organised by the Rump Presidency in Belgrade on the 3rd of January, 1992, with representatives of the leaderships of the SAOs in Croatia, the Bosnian Serbs and members of the SRS as well as other Serb parties, a slightly revised map of targeted areas evolved. And this map was actually published in the magazine Epoha on the 7th of January, 1992, and that will be Exhibit 1879. If you look at the light blue territories, these are actually the territories that at that time were pursued, and you can see that Dubrovnik Republik is gone. The Dubrovnik Republik is no longer light blue. And also Western Slavonia is basically also now dark blue and no more considered to be part of the plan. One point that I would like to point out. You'll find the word "Krajina" several times on the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could we zoom in on the screen so that whoever wants to watch this by video also has an opportunity to better follow what you're saying.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. You'll see, actually "Krajina" pointed here. That's here where just the marker is. That's the SAO -- the SAO -- the former SAO Krajina that at that time was already evolving into RSK. You'll find on top -- on top you'll find also "Krajina." That's referring to Eastern Slavonia, Baranja and Western Srem, and please do not confuse it with the autonomous region of Krajina. That's in Bosnia. What you can see is the Posavina Corridor, which is called here "SAO Semberija." You can see it here linking the territories within Bosnia and also the territory in Croatia to Serbia. That's all I want to say at this stage. We'll deal with this map during the trial. On the 9th of January, 1992, the Bosnian Serb Assembly proclaimed the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. In relation to its territories, it was stated that it included "areas where the Serbian people are a minority because of the genocide conducted against it in the Second World War." And that will be Exhibit 3012. Let me remind you that that is the terminology very similar to that used by Seselj when he refers to the Serbia graves as marking the borders of Greater Serbia. The evidence will show that throughout the indictment period, Seselj and the Bosnian Serb leadership pursued basically the same goals in relation to Bosnia and Herzegovina. Seselj had contacts with the Bosnian Serb leaders throughout the indictment period and even supported them in 1993 in their opposition to Milosevic regarding the Vance-Owen Plan. Here I want to give you one example, and it's Exhibit 2029, a speech that Mr. Seselj gave on the 11th of March, 1993. "We believe that no one has the right to accept the Vance-Owen ultimatum in the name of the Serbian people concerning the internal borders in the territory of the former Bosnia and Herzegovina. Particularly, we believe that no one has the right to give the corridor between Bosnian Krajina and Semberija to the Croats, the Muslims or UNPROFOR, in the same of the Serbian people. The Serbian Radical Party maintains its position that the only just and firm boundary determination in the territory of the former Bosnia and Herzegovina can be at the front lines reached." Over this issue, the accused finally split with Slobodan Milosevic, at least temporarily, and that is why the Prosecution restricted this indictment to the time period between the 1st of August, 1991, to September 1993. But let me go back to 1992. On 12 May 1992, during the 16th session of the Serbian Assembly, Radovan Karadzic pronounced the six strategic objectives of the Bosnian Serbs. However, these objectives were not established at that time. In May 1992, they had, in fact, been ruthlessly implemented in several municipalities by forces, including the SRS and SCP volunteers, namely, in Bosanski Samac, Bijeljina, Brcko, and Zvornik. What were these objectives? And I'll show you here Exhibit 74. It's the text of the objectives. First is, establish state borders separating the Serbian people from the other two ethnic communities. Second, set up a corridor between Semberija and Krajina. Third, establish a corridor in the Drina river valley, that is, eliminate the Drina as a border separating Serbian states. Four, establish a border at the Una and Neretva rivers. Five, divide the city of Sarajevo into Serbian and Muslim parts and establish effective state authorities in both parts. And six, ensure access to the sea for Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Uertz-Retzlaff, I see on what you've just shown us on television, that this was signed by Mr. Krajisnik, President of the Assembly. You earlier said the Serbian Assembly. Could you please always clearly indicate what assembly we're talking about. The Serbian Assembly could be the assembly of the Republic of Serbia, but from what I see, it seems that it might not be the assembly of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: No, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please always express yourself very clearly on these matters.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. The Serbian assembly of course in -- the Bosnian Serb Assembly. In that same session, on the 12th of March -- May, 1992, Karadzic also mentioned in relation to the first objective, that it meant the "separation from those who are our enemies and who have used every opportunity, especially in this century, to attack us, and who would continue with this practice if we were to stay together in the same state." And in relation to the second goal, he mentioned that "the second strategic goal is a corridor between Semberija and Krajina ... this is of utmost strategic importance for the Serbian people because it integrates the Serbian countries ... the alliance of Serbian states is infeasible if we do not secure this corridor ..." Now, Your Honour, I have now the map that you said we need to reconsider, but I have planned to show it and I can't change it right now. So here is actually indicated on this map the objective -- objectives that Karadzic spoke about. That map is Exhibit 3007. And the Assembly session that I just mentioned is the Assembly, Exhibit 241. And what was in store for the non-Serbs in Bosnia and Herzegovina is clearly stated by members of the JCE. At a session of the Assembly of Bosnia and Herzegovina, I mean now the official Assembly of Bosnia and Herzegovina, held on the 15th of October, 1991, the Assembly considered inter alia a platform on the position of Bosnia and Herzegovina in the future of Yugoslavia, and Radovan Karadzic said the following, that warned the Muslims if they persisted in pursuing independence: "This is the road that you want Bosnia and Herzegovina to take, the same highway to hell and suffering that Slovenia and Croatia went through. Don't think you won't take Bosnia and Herzegovina to hell and Muslim people to possible extinction." Now let me quote what Seselj put in writing in relation to the non-Serbs, and I have here a document 1261. It's actually from a chapter of his book, "In Sinisa Aksentijevic's Focus, Philippics of Chetnik's Vojvoda" regarding Septa was the headline, "treatment of non-Serbs in the process of unification ..." The headline is longer but I just referred to this part. And the accused said the following about the non-Serb population in the new Serb state: "That is inevitable formation of a civilian state, the state of the Serbs equal (loyalty is implicit) citizens, members of other nations, ethnic minorities and groups. If such state is formed, other nations, ethnic minorities and groups should not exceed more than 8% of the total population; they should not exceed the said percentage in any larger settlement, region or administrative unit, and there should be no possibility to change their percentage through birth rate." The text, of course, is much more complex, but I can only quote this for time reasons. Of course, this view made resettlement of huge numbers of non-Serbs necessary. The ethnic division on the ground that Karadzic and Seselj requested meant expulsion of non-Serbs from claimed territories. Even in territories dominated by Serbs, Muslims and Croats settlements had to be uprooted and the non-Serbs driven out in order to ensure a homogeneous territory. And I would like to show you briefly two maps that will be elaborated upon by our expert witness, Dr. Tabeau. The first one is actually a map showing Bosnia-Herzegovina's ethnic minority population roster, and as you can see, it's a patchwork picture in the municipalities. It's based on the census of 1991. And you can, in particular, see the Posavina Corridor, for instance, on the top. It would actually be partly Croat, partly mixed. So it's in quite a mixed territory with the populations. And now I show you a later map that also Ms. Tabeau will speak about. You can see here the effect of the conflict where you have basically very special, clearly defined territories along ethnic lines. The Serb forces executing the plan in Croatia and Bosnia-Herzegovina were basically the same in all territories, with some minor variations due to the circumstances on the ground. And also basically the same were the crimes. Our evidence will demonstrate beyond any doubt that the events in the municipalities and the towns and villages were not random or spontaneous acts of a few individuals but were the result of a policy pursued by the accused and others and implemented by forces under their control or influence. Let me now turn to the crimes committed in specific towns and municipalities. At the outset, let me say this: Many cases have been conducted and concluded in this court in which these crimes were addressed in detail. Eyewitnesses to the crimes, mostly victims, have described their ordeals and suffering. In this case, there is no need to hear much so-called crime-base evidence. Certain notorious criminal events, like the murder of the men from Vukovar hospital, the abuse of victims in camps throughout Bosnia-Herzegovina, are meanwhile common knowledge or at least adjudicated. In this trial, the Prosecution will therefore introduce crime-base evidence mostly in written form. The focus of this case will be evidence dealing with the structures that were utilised to commit the crimes and linking the accused to the crimes. Let me now first turn to the events in Vukovar. And I'll show you here a map of Vukovar. It's Exhibit 3127. And it depicts, basically, the places that you will hear about from the witnesses. It's the Vukovar hospital; Velepromet, a former economical complex; the JNA barracks; and on the bottom, Ovcara.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before you continue, Madam Uertz-Retzlaff, can you give us an idea on how much time you'd still need? Of course, I have to think about a break.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: It's quite -- I have basically more than half, I have done, but it's still ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then I suggest that we take a break now, and that we'll resume at five minutes past 1.00, and then have another 40 minutes this morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll adjourn until five minutes past 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Uertz-Retzlaff, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Before the break, we saw the town map of Vukovar with certain places indicated. It's actually map 19 in the trial binder. On the 18th of November, 1991, Vukovar fell to the Serb forces. An elderly man and his wife, fearing the worst, went to the hospital to find protection. The following day, the non-Serb men were taken away by Serb forces, threatened and cursed on their way, and eventually arrived at the Ovcara farm. There they were beaten by soldiers and subjected to all sorts of cruelty. Some were killed right there in front or in the hangar. The elderly man, who will be a witness together with a few others, survived because he knew one of the soldiers personally and that soldier saved his life. The other roughly 260 men and a few women were murdered and buried in a mass grave. What does this event have to do with the accused Seselj? The Prosecution will provide written and oral evidence that in 1991, the accused decided that the SRS should send as many volunteers as possible to Vukovar. The SRS/SCP volunteers sent to Vukovar were placed under the command of Milan Lancuzanin, also known as Kameni, commander of the Leva Supoderica detachment, and were subordinated to the TO and the JNA. Here you'll see a document. It's Exhibit 1415. It is a letter of the chief of the staff of the SRS war staff dated 9 November, 1991.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's still illegible to me. Is it my screen or ...

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: No, it's actually bad. Perhaps we can highlight --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If I don't watch it through the video but through the e-court, then I get it better.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At the same time, I wonder what will be provided to the accused. Therefore, I'll continue to watch video, and you should take care that by zooming in or out, that one could follow that also, if one receives a video, rather than to use the e-court facilities available here. So I now move back to the video and ...

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And you can see here, it's from the Serbian Radical Party War Staff --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If it will be on our screen, then I'll be able to see that on the video. Could we move to the document with the assistance of the technicians.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: It's actually there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, it's not on the -- if you use the video, which is the one -- there now, there we are. Could it be zoomed in in such a way that we can read the relevant portions.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: So you see the body of the text. What you can't see right now is -- it's from the SRS War Staff, and it is addressed to the commander of the Leva Supoderica detachment, referring to the subordination of the volunteers to the Vukovar TO. And mentioned in the first paragraph, I'm referring here particularly to the first and second paragraph, there is mentioning of two other members of the SRS - that's Slobodan Katic, who gets is -- is mentioned here as a commander, and also you have mentioned in the second paragraph Branislav Vakic from Nis, who is also appointed commander. I don't want to go into more specifics of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that once it will be introduced in evidence, then we'll get both versions, and legible for everyone.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The Prosecution will provide testimony of soldiers regarding the cooperation of the man Kameni with the commanders of the TO and the JNA Guards Brigade in Vukovar. The accused himself said on TV Benkovac on the 23rd of November, 1991 - and that will be Exhibit 734 - that "Kameni, our main commander in Vukovar, plans his action with the army major in the evening and executes it the next day. The army did not have enough manpower to go around capturing each house because of desertion - that is what our men did." A few days before the massacre at Ovcara, the accused came to Vukovar in order to visit the volunteers and boost their morale. He participated in a meeting with the TO and the JNA commanders. During his visit in Vukovar, the accused said the following: "We are all one army. This war is a great test for Serbs. Those who pass the test will become winners. Deserters cannot go unpunished. Not a single Ustasha must leave Vukovar alive." And the soldiers did what Seselj had requested them to do. When the Serb forces occupied the city, hundreds of Croats were killed by Serb forces. Among those committing the murders at Vukovar and in Ovcara and elsewhere in Vukovar were the SRS/SCP volunteers, commanded by Kameni. Let me show you a photo - Exhibit 2441 - that shows the accused in the destroyed Vukovar. And to his left, the man with the cap, that is the man Kameni, Lancuzanin, the commander of the Leva Supoderica detachment. We will hear from witnesses present at the Ovcara farm, Vukovar hospital, the barracks and Ovcara that the SRS/SCP volunteers led by Kameni wanted revenge on those taken from the Vukovar hospital. The evidence will show that many SRS/SCP volunteers participated in the mass murder at Ovcara. And we will hear from witnesses that the man Kameni was a close associate of the accused. He had direct access to the accused and reported to him personally. Kameni was recently convicted and sentenced to 20 years' imprisonment in Belgrade for his participation in the atrocities at Ovcara farm. And I will show you now a photo of Kameni. He is here under number 8. Under number 8 you can see the man Kameni. And I'll show you another photo. Photo -- showing the person inter alia, Branislav Vakic, who was also mentioned in the order that you saw previously. There's a question mark behind the name "Vakic". That's from an earlier stage. The witness -- you will see witnesses who clearly identify this person. The accused, on the 13th of May, 1993, promoted Kameni and Vakic to the rank of Chetnik Vojvoda for their achievement during the Vukovar campaign and elsewhere. And the photos that you saw are from the ceremony appointing these Vojvodas. And I will show you the document that I mentioned already earlier. That's the promotion order number 124. You can see here, on top of it there is the order, 124, and when you look at number 3, you see here that Branislav Vakic is promoted. He is called "Chetnik Major" in this paragraph. It says: "In April 1991 he was in Borovo Selo. He participated in the liberation of Vukovar as deputy commander of the Leva Supoderica volunteer unit. He also commanded the Serbian Chetnik units in Serbian Herzegovina in May and June 1992." There are a references made to a lot of places, including Mostar. And under number 10, you see a description of Milan Lancuzanin, Kameni, and I only want to draw your attention to the fact that he's actually mentioned as the best of the best, and the excellent commander of the Leva Supoderica detachment. What the order does not say but what the evidence will show is that wherever these two Vojvodas were active in the field, non-Serbs were murdered. These two are not the only perpetrators of crimes against humanity who were promoted by the accused on that occasion, on the 13th of May, 1993. I will come to this later. Topola, another SRS/SCP volunteer - his nickname is Topola - was also present at Ovcara farm. He killed Croats also elsewhere in Vukovar, including Velepromet, a commercial complex close to the JNA barracks, used by the Serb forces as a detention facility. After the fall of Vukovar, Topola and some other SRS/SCP volunteers removed detainees from the room where they were detained and killed them. That's a separate charge in the indictment related to Vukovar. The evidence will show that when Seselj was informed about the crimes committed by Topola, he simply said: "What can I do? Disarm the man and send him home. He is tired." The excused or his associates did not report these crimes to the Serbian authorities in Belgrade. Instead, they later sent Topola as a volunteer to Bosnia and Herzegovina, where he again committed serious crimes against the non-Serb population. Let me now briefly turn to Western Slavonia, and in particular, Vocin in the Podravska Slatina municipality. That's the map 2 in the binder. I just want to indicate to you where Podravska Slatina is situated. As you can see, it's right east of Virovitica. Looking at this map, it is obvious that if Seselj and others wanted the JCE to establish the borders of Greater Serbia along the Karlobag-Ogulin-Karlovac-Virovitica line, they needed to control the Podravska Slatina municipality. And if they wanted a homogeneous Greater Serbia, they needed to expel the Croatian population which amounted to 1.500 inhabitants in Vocin. And this is what, indeed, was done from August to December 1991, when the Serb forces were in control in Vocin. What connects the accused to these events? The JNA neither did have the manpower to engage its units in this part of Western Slavonia or did not want to. The evidence will show that the other JCE members, in particular Slobodan Milosevic, did not pay much attention to Western Slavonia. It was the accused who took a particular interest in the take-over of this territory. Throughout the fall of 1991, the SRS sent hundreds of hundreds of volunteers to Western Slavonia. Had they not been brought to Western Slavonia by Seselj, and had they not terrorised the non-Serb population, both the Croats and the Serbs would have been a -- suffering of both the Croats and the Serbs would have been avoided. The Prosecution will not lead any crime-base evidence. However, we will show, in relation to this particular place, how close and how effective the SRS and the TO in Western Slavonia and elsewhere coordinated their actions. I want to show you four documents in a row. The first one is a request of the Western Slavonia TO, of the 12th of October, 1991, asking the SRS headquarters in Belgrade for the provision of volunteers. The next document is actually the reaction of the SRS War Staff of the 16th of October, approving the dispatch of volunteers but asking for certain technical matters in relation to the troops, about their accommodation and the like. The next document -- and I forgot to say, that's actually Exhibit 1413. Exhibit 1414 is, again, a letter of the TO Western Slavonia to the SRS, from the 19th of October, 1991, actually, addressing these particular technical matters that were raised. And a few days later, volunteers were dispatched with their SRS and SCP commander. And I'll show you here the next document. It's the Exhibit 2144. It's an authorisation of the 24th of October, 1991. Zoran Rankic, the Deputy Chief of the SRS War Staff, informs the Podravska Slatina TO staff that Radovan Novacic was authorised "on behalf of the SRS volunteer units" to coordinate with them. These documents show that within two weeks, volunteers, including a commander, were dispatched after a TO request. And that is just one example of how the SRS headquarters, the JNA, and the local authorities acted "hand in glove" throughout the conflict in Croatia and Bosnia-Herzegovina. In this context, let me refer again to the basic military organisation of the Serbian Radical Party volunteers. I have already shown you this document briefly, and it's Exhibit 1261. And I would like to draw your attention to Rule number 7, where it says that "the volunteers of the Serbian Radical Party are engaged in combat and other combat-related activities independently or as part of the appropriate unit of the JNA, army of Republika Srpska, or army of Serbian Krajina, according to the plans made by the commands of the aforementioned armies. "Volunteer units are engaged in these armies only in their entirety and under the command of the volunteer commanders, exceptions possible if arranged." In this connection, a volunteer commander, in full authority and responsibility, is delegated to the specific command to coordinate possibilities, requests, requirements, utilisation, and security of the volunteer units. And now let's go to paragraph 11, where the hierarchial command structure in the SRS is described as follows: "The Commands of the Serbian Radical Party Volunteers are organised as commanding organs for all volunteer forces, their units and their combat activities. They are formed analogously to commanding structure of the party organs. The Homeland Command, commands of military districts and commands of units." And I told you in the beginning that Vojislav Seselj was actually the chief of the Homeland Command. Witnesses will tell us that at times the SRS transferred volunteers of its party and other volunteers together to the front lines. For the local population, the volunteers were just the same. Their presence created a climate of fear by looting, threatening, abusing and killing civilians. And what is important: They all considered themselves Chetniks and associated themselves with the accused's goal of Greater Serbia. Again, in relation to Vocin, in November 1991, the accused visited Vocin and met his volunteers, and we will hear from local witnesses that the volunteers, after meeting Seselj, became more aggressive and there was a sharp increase of crimes against Croat civilians after this visit. In general, the SRS/SCP volunteers were widely known for their brutality and ruthlessness. The Prosecution will provide numerous documents from the military, the police and from NGOs that the bad reputation of the SRS/SCP volunteers were not based on myth but based on facts. And I will show you only one example and -- for Croatia. That's a letter from Helsinki Watch, from the 21st of January, 1992. It is Exhibit 1418. I just draw your attention to page 2, paragraph 3, where it says the following: "The Serbian government has also condoned and, in some cases, supported the formation of at least three paramilitary groups in Serbia which operate in Croatia. What appears to be the most brutal of these groups is led by Vojislav Seselj, leader of the Serbian Radical Party and the Serbian Chetnik Movement. Seselj's group of paramilitaries call themselves Chetniks and operate throughout Croatia." That will do. Just to mention the two other groups that are referred to in this letter were actually Arkan's men and Mirko Jovic's group, often remembered to as White Eagles. And now one example for Bosnia and Herzegovina. It is Exhibit 1339. And it is a report prepared by the Main Staff of the VRS, on the 28th of July, 1992, and the document -- report prepared is entitled "Report on Paramilitary Formations in the Territory of Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina." It reads as follows, and I quote: "They are mostly composed of individuals of low moral quality, and in many cases of persons previously prosecuted for crimes and offences and even convicted of murder, robbery, larceny and the like. Very often, such units have in their ranks pathological criminals whom the conditions of war and general lawlessness have brought to the fore. Many formations of this type display hatred of non-Serbian peoples and one can conclude without reservations that they are the genocidal elements among the Serbian people. War profiteering and looting are the motive for the great majority of the paramilitaries ..." And another point: "One common feature of all paramilitary formations is that they do not take part in direct fighting with the enemy. Instead, they are operating behind the lines of the regular Serbian Republic Bosnian Army units, looting and burning property and killing the innocent civilian population." This report identifies various groups, but they name also Seseljevci or Seselj's men, a term often used for the SRS/SCP volunteers. The Prosecution will provide evidence that the accused Seselj was fully apprised of the types of people that joined the ranks of the SRS and SCP volunteers, and other volunteers he assisted in transferring to the regions. Both the SRS members and local officials informed the accused and his associates in the SRS office in Belgrade about the unruly and cruel behaviour of the volunteers on the ground. Those providing such information to the accused were met with indifference or even hostility. The accused was fully aware about the events on the front. His staff in the region and in Belgrade kept him constantly informed. During his many visits to the front lines both in Croatia and Bosnia and Herzegovina, the accused would see with his own eyes the destruction done by the Serb forces on Muslim and Croat settlements. As a high-ranking politician and member of the Serbian parliament, the accused, of course, had many means of receiving information. And let us not forget, a large amount of information about military actions and crimes was in the public domain. Now let me turn to Bosnia and Herzegovina, and in particular, Bosanski Samac -- just in passing, Bosanski Samac, Bijeljina, and Brcko. I have already mentioned the speech of Radovan Karadzic of the 12th of May, 1992, stressing the crucial importance of the corridor. The Serb leadership in Serbia and RSK were equally aware of the importance of the Posavina Corridor as the lifeline to the Serbian motherland. Therefore, members of the JCE from all territories and institutions were involved in the planning, preparation, and execution of the military operations in the corridor, including the accused Seselj. And I'm just pointing out here the map -- the map number 2 in the binder, where you can see that Bosanski Samac, Brcko, and Bijeljina lie in that corridor. And there's also -- you can also already see that Zvornik is also important for the corridor and for the goal in relation to the Drina River. These three municipalities are -- before the war, the majority population in Bosanski Samac was of Croat ethnicity; in Brcko, Muslims had the majority; and in Bijeljina, the majority was Serb. However, in all three locations, the same things happened. From April 1992 onwards, non-Serbs were expelled from these municipalities by force. The Prosecution will not hear any crime-base witnesses. Some witnesses, however, will address the events there in general terms. And their evidence will show that the attack on the non-Serb population in Bosnia and Herzegovina actually started in Bijeljina. In these three municipalities that are mentioned, the local authorities as well as the Bosnian Serb leadership requested that the SRS send volunteers to these municipalities. And, indeed, SRS volunteers did arrive and participated in the initial attack on these locations and also in the crimes that followed. To Bosanski Samac, the SRS War Staff sent volunteers that were led by Srecko Radovanovic, Debeli. And you see him here on this photo that's Exhibit 3117 -- 3017. He is there on the right side. And in Brcko and Bijeljina, Mirko Blagojevic was in charge of the SRS/SCP volunteers. And you see him here, the man with the typical Serbian hat and kokarda. The SRS/SCP volunteers fought alongside JNA units, Bosnian Serb TO, members of the Serbian MUP and Arkan's Tigers. The Prosecution will provide evidence that the accused was informed about the violent events in the said municipalities, yet he promoted those two that I mentioned to Vojvodas. And it's actually the same promotion order that you saw previously here. Mr. Debeli -- Debeli is the nickname. Debeli is here under number 15, Srecko Radovanovic is mentioned here, and he is mentioned as a Chetnik colonel who organised and trained Chetnik units. He is mentioned as being a participant in Croatia from April 1992, and then in Bosnia inter alia Bosanski Samac and Brcko are mentioned. And number 2 of that same order shows Mirko Blagojevic, who is mentioned in relation to the entire Semberija, in particular, Bijeljina, Zvornik and Brcko. I have already shown you where Zvornik is situated and how important it was for both the goal in relation to the corridor and the third goal in relation to the Drina River. The events in this municipality illustrate, in the most shocking way, the pattern that unfolded through Bosnia-Herzegovina. To get firm control over Zvornik, the members of the JCE had to expel in particular the Muslim population that made up 59% of the population in Zvornik in 1991. By March 1992, the Bosnian Serbs had established their own police force in Zvornik, had declared Zvornik a Serbian municipality, and were preparing the attack on Zvornik. Beginning in April, Serb forces attacked Muslims and Croats living in town, villages, and small settlements, most of which were undefended and contained no military targets. Muslims and Croats were mistreated and killed during the attack, and even more so during the persecution campaign that unfolded afterwards. The non-Serb population, mostly men, were arrested and taken to various detention facilities. The conditions in the detention facilities were horrible. Many detainees were beaten, tortured and killed. They were also forced to work. And thousands of non-Serbs, mostly Muslims, were expelled from their municipality. Their homes were looted and destroyed as well as religious and cultural monuments. And just here, a map -- a town map of Zvornik, with the detention facilities shown. You can see it also on the map 22 that you have in the map binder, where you can see the photos better. The Prosecution will provide evidence of the massacre of 88 Muslim males at Drinjaca Dom Kulture between the 30th and the 31st of May, 1992; the killing of 150 men at the Karakaj Technical School, between 7 and 9 June; the massacre of 150 Muslim males at Gero's slaughterhouse between 7 and 9 June; and the murder of more than 14 non-Serb detainees between the 1st and the 26th of June, at Celopek Dom Culture. These figures alone show clearly the extraordinary brutality the non-Serb population was subjected to in Zvornik. Why is the accused charged with these crimes? In March 1992, while the Bosnian Serbs were preparing the attack, the accused gave a speech in Mali Zvornik, just across the Drina River from Zvornik, and he declared: "Dear Chetnik brothers, especially you across the Drina River, you are the bravest ones. We are going to clean Bosnia of pagans and show them a road which will take them to the east, where they belong." In April 1992, Branko Grujic, the president of the Crisis Staff in Zvornik, requested SRS volunteers to come to Zvornik, and the accused personally approved this request. We will hear from witnesses that SRS leaders brought SRS volunteers from Loznica, commanded by Dragan Cvetinovic, to Zvornik. Subsequently, when the war broke out, local Serbs joined those SRS/SCP volunteers. You will also hear evidence that SRS/SCP volunteers took part in the violent takeover of Zvornik town and fought alongside Arkan's Tigers, the local TO and the JNA and police forces. The SRS/SCP volunteers were commanded by Miroslav Vukovic, also known as Cele. Both Miroslav Vukovic and Dragan Cvetinovic were promoted in the same order that you now saw a couple of times. Mr. Vukovic is under number 5. He's named as the commander of the units of the Serbian Chetnik Movement and the SRS in Slavonia, Baranja and Western Srem. And he's also mentioned in eastern Slavonia. And we have number 16, Dragan Cvetinovic, who is mentioned as commander of the Chetniks -- Chetnik unit from Loznica. We also have the photos of these two persons. One is Exhibit 3036. We see here in the middle, Miroslav Vukovic, and we have the photo of Cvetinovic as well. And he is seen here next to Mirko Blagojevic. The Prosecution will provide evidence that the SRS and SCP volunteers took part in every mass killing that I just mentioned. Many witnesses will refer to the crimes committed by the Yellow Wasps, and the Prosecution will provide witness evidence that the so-called Yellow Wasps, led by the Vuckovic brothers, were SRS/SCP volunteers to begin with. They had joined the SRS in 1991 and had been indoctrinated by Seselj's hate propaganda. They had fought already in Croatia, and it was the SRS headquarters in Belgrade that brought them to Zvornik. Finally, the Prosecution will provide evidence that throughout the fighting and the persecution campaign in Zvornik, the accused was regularly provided with information by SRS officials around Zvornik. Some of the proceeds from the looting went to the fund of the SRS in Belgrade.

utterances.text: Madam Uertz-Retzlaff, I'm looking at the clock. It's a quarter to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So we have to finish for the day. You used, until now, approximately 1 hour and 40 minutes, which means that there are 50 minutes remaining for tomorrow. Two and a half hours.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. In relation to what I have to say, but there's also --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, no, the Prosecution was granted two and a half hours for the opening statement. The 8th of November, Status Conference, I think I said the Prosecution should not take more than two and a half hours for its opening statement, which means 150 minutes. You've used 100 minutes by now, so another 50 minutes remaining.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes, that's right. I misheard. I heard you say 15 minutes, and I was thinking how can we finish. Sorry. I misheard, 50 minutes that's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So that means we'll resume tomorrow morning at 9.00, in this same courtroom, and you'll then have until ten minutes to 10.00 to finalise your opening statement. We'll then, depending on whether Mr. Seselj is in this court or not, hear his unsworn statement. Since we have to take an early break tomorrow, if we will not finish tomorrow, as I said before, we will then continue on Friday afternoon. We stand adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 28th day of November, 2006, at 9.00 a.m.
